name: claude-profiles
description: Run two or more Claude Code subscriptions side by side on one machine — work and personal, or client and your own — each with its own login, rate limits and session history, while they share one set of settings, plugins, skills, agents, commands, hooks and MCP servers. The setup-claude-profiles skill explains the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR model, then does the work with three python3 scripts: a read-only doctor that reports every profile with its account, plan, credential store and platform hazards; an idempotent, dry-run-first linker that shares config by symlink (including the @-imports a CLAUDE.md pulls in) and can undo itself from its own backups; and an MCP mirror, because mcpServers lives in .claude.json — the one file that also holds the account and so can never be shared. Covers macOS, Linux and WSL + Ubuntu, where the config directory must stay off the Windows drive or symlinks and the 0600 mode on the credentials file silently fail. Knows the traps that look like success: the stale ~/.claude/.claude.json that reports the wrong account, the marketplace registry split across settings.json and plugins/known_marketplaces.json, a shared status line with an email hardcoded in it, and a shell inside a session inheriting CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Needs python3.
